statement: Carbon commonly forms four covalent-bond contributions in neutral organic frameworks, enabling chains, branches and rings.
scope_limits: C03 retains generic bonding and molecular-geometry foundations; C06 owns organic-chemistry application of carbon frameworks.

statement: A carbon–carbon single bond contains one sigma bond, whereas double and triple bonds add one or two pi-bond components respectively. In the introductory hybridization model, carbon centers are commonly described as sp3 with approximately tetrahedral local geometry, sp2 with trigonal-planar geometry, or sp with linear geometry; a pi bond also restricts free rotation compared with an ordinary isolated sigma bond.
scope_limits: Hybridization is used as a chemistry-facing model, not as a replacement for C03 bonding/geometry or deeper electronic-structure theory.

statement: Line-angle formulas encode carbon connectivity compactly while leaving many carbon-bound hydrogen atoms implicit.
scope_limits: C03 retains generic bonding and molecular-geometry foundations; C06 owns organic-chemistry application of carbon frameworks.

statement: Conjugation permits electron density to be described across adjacent p-orbital sites rather than as isolated localized pi bonds.
scope_limits: C03 retains generic bonding and molecular-geometry foundations; C06 owns organic-chemistry application of carbon frameworks.

statement: Resonance structures are alternative contributors to one electronic structure and should not be interpreted as isolable structures in rapid equilibrium.
scope_limits: C03 retains generic bonding and molecular-geometry foundations; C06 owns organic-chemistry application of carbon frameworks.

statement: A functional group is a recurring structural motif used to classify organic compounds and organize characteristic chemical behavior.
scope_limits: C03 retains general intermolecular-force/structure foundations; C04 retains generic acid–base/equilibrium ownership.

statement: Alcohols contain a hydroxyl group attached to carbon, whereas ethers contain an oxygen atom bonded to two carbon groups. Their oxygen-containing functional groups influence polarity and hydrogen-bond donor/acceptor behavior, so functional-group identity can help explain intermolecular-property trends without serving as a universal single-factor rule.
scope_limits: C03 retains general intermolecular-force foundations; C06 applies them to organic functional groups.

statement: A carbonyl group is present in aldehydes and ketones and is also embedded within carboxylic acids and their derivatives. Carbonyl polarization helps organize characteristic reactivity, while the acidic behavior of carboxylic acids reflects the full molecular context and conjugate-base stabilization rather than the label 'carbonyl' alone.
scope_limits: C04 retains generic acid–base/equilibrium ownership; C06 owns organic structure–reactivity interpretation.

statement: Amines and amides both contain nitrogen, but resonance with an adjacent carbonyl makes amide nitrogen electronically and chemically distinct from ordinary amine nitrogen; ordinary amines are therefore often substantially more basic than analogous amides under comparable conditions.
scope_limits: Uses C04 acid–base foundations to explain organic functional-group trends without claiming a universal pKa ranking.

statement: Systematic organic nomenclature encodes a parent framework, principal functional group and substituent positions so that a structure can be communicated unambiguously within stated conventions.
scope_limits: C03 retains general intermolecular-force/structure foundations; C04 retains generic acid–base/equilibrium ownership.

statement: Curved-arrow notation in organic mechanisms represents the movement of electron pairs from an electron source toward an electron-deficient destination.
scope_limits: C04 retains general kinetics/equilibrium and overall reaction ownership; C06 owns organic electron-flow mechanism models.

statement: A nucleophile donates an electron pair in bond formation, whereas an electrophile accepts electron density at an electron-poor site. A leaving group is an atom or group that departs from a substrate with the bonding electron pair in the common heterolytic bookkeeping model; leaving-group ability depends on molecular and reaction context.
scope_limits: Foundational organic mechanism vocabulary; no universal nucleophilicity/electrophilicity/leaving-group ranking is asserted.

statement: An elementary mechanistic step must maintain chemically consistent atom and charge bookkeeping even when formal charges change location.
scope_limits: C04 retains general kinetics/equilibrium and overall reaction ownership; C06 owns organic electron-flow mechanism models.

statement: Substitution, addition and elimination are broad reaction-pattern classes distinguished by how bonds and substituents change, not by one universal mechanism.
scope_limits: C04 retains general kinetics/equilibrium and overall reaction ownership; C06 owns organic electron-flow mechanism models.

statement: Mechanistic proposals are constrained by experimental evidence such as kinetics, stereochemical outcomes and product distributions; a balanced overall equation alone is insufficient.
scope_limits: C04 retains general kinetics/equilibrium and overall reaction ownership; C06 owns organic electron-flow mechanism models.

statement: Constitutional isomers have the same molecular formula but different atomic connectivity, whereas stereoisomers have the same atomic connectivity and differ in the three-dimensional arrangement of atoms.
scope_limits: C03 retains generic geometry/structure; C06 owns organic stereochemical classification.

statement: Enantiomers are nonsuperposable mirror-image stereoisomers, whereas diastereomers are stereoisomers that are not mirror-image partners. Enantiomers often share many bulk properties in achiral environments but can interact differently with chiral reagents, catalysts, receptors or other chiral environments.
scope_limits: Chemistry-facing chiral-environment consequence only; biological conclusions remain outside this node.

statement: The R/S descriptor records an absolute configuration according to CIP priority rules and does not specify the sign of optical rotation.
scope_limits: C03 retains generic geometry/structure; instrument-specific chiral analysis remains C05 background.

statement: E/Z descriptors distinguish alkene configurations when each double-bond carbon bears two different priority groups.
scope_limits: C03 retains generic geometry/structure; instrument-specific chiral analysis remains C05 background.

statement: Conformations connected by rotation about ordinary single bonds can interconvert without bond breaking, while configurational interconversion generally requires a different structural process. A stereoselective process forms stereoisomeric products in unequal proportions; a racemic mixture contains equal amounts of a pair of enantiomers, whereas non-racemic samples have unequal enantiomeric composition.
scope_limits: Foundational stereochemical composition and selectivity only; specialist chiral analysis remains C05 background and biological efficacy is not inferred.

statement: A forward synthetic sequence identifies starting material, reagents or conditions, intermediates and products, while retrosynthetic analysis reasons backward from a target structure by proposing strategic disconnections that correspond to plausible forward transformations.
scope_limits: Foundational synthesis-route vocabulary and retrosynthetic reasoning; manufacturing process design remains future boundary-only.

statement: Functional-group interconversion changes one functional group into another while preserving the intended carbon framework unless the route explicitly changes that framework.
scope_limits: C05 retains analytical-method ownership; future specialized manufacturing/material scopes remain boundary-only.

statement: Chemoselectivity is preferential reaction at one functional group or reactive site in the presence of alternatives; regioselectivity is preferential formation or reaction at one constitutional position, while stereoselectivity concerns unequal formation of stereoisomeric outcomes. These selectivities depend on substrate, reagent, conditions and competing pathways.
scope_limits: Foundational synthesis selectivity vocabulary; no universal reagent-selection table is asserted.

statement: Overall isolated yield across a multistep linear sequence is limited multiplicatively by the yields of individual steps.
scope_limits: C05 retains analytical-method ownership; future specialized manufacturing/material scopes remain boundary-only.

statement: A defensible synthetic route balances feasibility, chemoselectivity/regioselectivity/stereochemical control, functional-group compatibility, cumulative yield, step economy, safety/resource constraints and purification rather than optimizing a single metric alone.
scope_limits: Route-level chemistry reasoning only; industrial process engineering and manufacturing remain future boundary-only.

statement: Structure–activity relationship analysis compares changes in molecular structure with changes in measured biological activity to guide chemical hypotheses.
scope_limits: C06 owns chemistry-facing molecular design; biological mechanism, clinical efficacy and health guidance lie outside this CURRICULUM child.

statement: Medicinal-chemistry optimization commonly balances potency and selectivity with physicochemical and ADME-relevant molecular properties such as solubility, lipophilicity, ionization state and metabolic stability, while also considering stereochemistry and synthetic accessibility; maximizing potency alone is not a sufficient optimization rule.
scope_limits: Chemistry-facing lead-optimization factors only; pharmacology, clinical efficacy and health guidance remain outside this CURRICULUM child.

statement: Ionizable functional groups influence charge state as a function of pH, which can affect solubility, permeability and molecular interactions.
scope_limits: C06 owns chemistry-facing molecular design; biological mechanism, clinical efficacy and health guidance lie outside this CURRICULUM child.

statement: Stereochemistry can change target interactions because biological binding environments are three-dimensional and often chiral.
scope_limits: C06 owns chemistry-facing molecular design; biological mechanism, clinical efficacy and health guidance lie outside this CURRICULUM child.

statement: An in-vitro active compound is not thereby established as a safe or effective medicine; medicinal-chemistry evidence is one component of a broader development process.
scope_limits: C06 owns chemistry-facing molecular design; biological mechanism, clinical efficacy and health guidance lie outside this CURRICULUM child.

statement: A monomer is a molecular starting unit capable of incorporation into a polymer; a polymer is a macromolecular substance composed of many constitutional repeating units, and a polymer sample generally contains molecules spanning a distribution of chain sizes. Polymer architectures may be linear, branched or crosslinked/networked.
scope_limits: Foundational polymer vocabulary and architecture; specialized materials engineering remains boundary-only.

statement: Chain-growth polymerization proceeds through active chain centers that add monomer sequentially, whereas step-growth polymerization builds larger species through reactions among functional groups on molecules of many sizes.
scope_limits: C06 owns polymer chemistry fundamentals; specialized materials engineering, industrial processing and future chemistry scopes remain boundary-only.

statement: Number-average and mass-average molar masses summarize different weightings of a polymer molecular-mass distribution and need not be equal.
scope_limits: C06 owns polymer chemistry fundamentals; specialized materials engineering, industrial processing and future chemistry scopes remain boundary-only.

statement: Branching, crosslinking, stereoregularity and copolymer sequence/architecture can alter packing, mobility and therefore material-property trends even when overall composition is similar. Polymerization conditions and control strategies can influence chain length, branching and architecture, but detailed reactor/process control remains outside this scope.
scope_limits: Chemistry-facing polymer structure–property/control relations only; materials/process engineering remains boundary-only.

statement: Polymer sustainability claims require attention to feedstocks, additives, processing, use, collection and end-of-life pathways. Recyclability and degradation depend on polymer chemistry together with contamination, additives, infrastructure and conditions; chemical structure alone does not determine total environmental performance or guarantee practical recycling/biodegradation.
scope_limits: Foundational chemistry of recyclability/degradation claims; lifecycle policy and industrial processing remain future boundaries.
